entries.title: Check for Updates in the app menu
entries.detail: The unus menu, at the left of the menu bar, has Check for Updates… under Settings…, in the same order as the menu bar icon's menu.

entries.title: What's New looks like j4k's
entries.detail: What's New shows a card for each day, as in j4k. When you check for updates and one is there, its changes show in the same window, with Install and Relaunch.

entries.title: About has a Docs button
entries.detail: About › Docs… opens the unus Field Manual in your browser: what unus understands, with examples to try.

entries.title: The shortcut puts the cursor at the bottom
entries.detail: When the shortcut brings the sheet up, the cursor waits at the end, on an empty line, ready for the next sum. If the last line has text, a new line is made under it; an empty one is used as it is.

entries.title: Settings look like scripta's
entries.detail: Settings has the same look as in scripta now: each box ends with one grey line that says what it does. Precision and the hotkey have a box each, and Start unus at login says what it does too.

entries.title: Updates look the same in every app
entries.detail: Settings › General ends with Updates now, the same in all four apps: Check Now and an Automatic switch in one row, and under it what the last check found.

entries.title: A Dock icon, and a choice where unus shows itself
entries.detail: unus has a Dock icon now, beside its icon in the menu bar. Settings › General chooses where it shows itself: the menu bar and the Dock, the menu bar alone, or the Dock alone. A click on the Dock icon opens the calculator, and its menu has the items of the menu bar menu.

entries.title: A pasted number with apostrophes counts
entries.detail: Paste 1’234’567 from a web page or from Word and unus answered 567: the apostrophe in it only LOOKS like the one unus writes. Four of those look-alikes count as thousands separators now, and a pasted number is tidied to one spelling. A space between the groups is still not a separator.

entries.title: After an update, What's New opens once
entries.detail: When unus has updated itself, the What's New window opens one time, so you see what changed without looking for it.

entries.title: An update says what is new, and a bad one is undone
entries.detail: When a new build is offered, the message lists what changed for you, from What's New. And when a new build does not stay open after an update, unus puts the build you had back and tells you.

entries.title: A hyphen inside a word is not a minus
entries.detail: x-ray 80 answered -80, and 2-bedroom flat 1800 answered -1'798: each hyphen was a subtraction. A word with a hyphen is one word now. 10-5 is still 5, and rate-tax still subtracts when you defined both names.

entries.title: unus reads back what it prints
entries.detail: A result you copy and paste into a line is the same amount again. Three kinds were not: tonnes (1'000 t), torque (N·m, lb·ft) and light minutes. A date that a sum moves past the year 9999, or before the year 1, shows a ? and no longer a wrong year.

entries.title: A refused line says why
entries.detail: A line that unus cannot answer, such as 5 km in kg or 5 / 0, shows a dim ? where the result would be. Point at the ? and the top bar says why. A line of plain text shows nothing, as before.

entries.title: Nine sentences answer right
entries.detail: These lines gave a wrong answer, and are right now: twenty five percent of 80 · one and a half hours · 120 less 10% · dinner 84 tip 20% · 3 nights at $120 · 12 payments of 99 · 6 ft 2 in cm · 1st of october · tomorrow at 3pm. An amount in parts is one amount: 2 h 45 min, 1 kg 200 g. The docs in the sheet show an example of each.

entries.title: About shows the kit version
entries.detail: The About window has a new row, Kit. It names the version of the code that unus shares with murmur, scripta and GLaDOS.

entries.title: Qwen holds less memory
entries.detail: With the Qwen model, unus held about 5 GB of memory. It now holds about 3 GB, at the same speed. After ten minutes without a translation, Qwen leaves memory; the next ⌘⏎ then takes about 4 seconds.

entries.title: Settings is as wide as in murmur, scripta and GLaDOS
entries.detail: The Settings window is wider, in both tabs. It now has the same width in all four apps.

entries.title: The Settings window keeps moving
entries.detail: After a drag on the tabs of the Settings window, a drag on its top no longer moved the window. Now a drag on the empty part of the top, beside the tabs, always moves it.

entries.title: What's New shows its scroll bar
entries.detail: When this window opens, the list shows its scroll bar, so you see that it goes on below.

entries.title: What's New
entries.detail: This window. About unus opens it, with the What's New… button beside the Settings… button.

entries.title: A Settings button in About
entries.detail: About unus has a Settings… button at the bottom. It opens the Settings window.

entries.title: Settings has a Brain tab
entries.detail: Settings has two tabs, General and Brain. The ⌘⏎ switch and the model picker are on the Brain tab. The text there has the scores measured on macOS 27, and it says that the Qwen model holds about 5 GB of memory while it is chosen.

entries.title: An update leaves no disk behind
entries.detail: After an update, the disk image it came on stayed open on this Mac. The updater now ejects it before it starts the new unus.

entries.title: Show unus in the menu, and a red shortcut when it is taken
entries.detail: The menu bar menu has a Show unus row, with the shortcut beside it. In Settings, the shortcut's label turns red when another app holds the same keys; hold the pointer on it to read why. A new sheet opens in front of the app you were in.

entries.title: The menu's windows open in front
entries.detail: About and Settings open in front of the app you were in. Before, a window could open behind it, and the menu row looked dead.

entries.title: ⌘H hides unus
entries.detail: ⌘H hides the sheet, as in every other app, and the shortcut brings it back. Hide Others and Show All are in the same menu.

entries.title: The shortcut works after a login
entries.detail: After a login, the shortcut could do nothing until unus was started again. It now makes the sheet when there is none.
